findings.failure_scenario: POST /v1/scrape with url "http://user:pass@example.com/page?q=1": before this change the schema returned a 400 (checkUrl's colon-count guard rejects userinfo URLs); now the preprocess returns "http://example.com/page?q=1", passes validation, and the scraper fetches the URL without credentials, returning a 401/login page while the caller believes the authenticated resource was scraped.
findings.summary: Rebuilding URLs that have a query string from urlObj.origin silently strips embedded credentials (user:pass@), so authenticated URLs are accepted but scraped without auth instead of being rejected.

findings.failure_scenario: url.parse('https://example.com/docs?page=2#section-3') returns 'https://example.com/docs?page=2'; the scrape job payload, crawl originUrl, and the returned document's metadata.sourceURL all lose the fragment the client submitted (e.g. Chrome 'copy link to highlight' URLs with #:~:text=...), so responses reference a different URL than the one requested.
findings.summary: Rebuilding the URL from origin+pathname+query silently drops the fragment (#...), altering the URL handed to the pipeline and reported back to the user.

findings.failure_scenario: 'https://example.com/path?a=1;b=2' becomes 'https://example.com/path?a=1%3Bb=2' (a server splitting params on ';' now sees one param instead of two); '?q=50%' becomes '?q=50%25'; '?q=%41' becomes '?q=A'; '?flag' becomes '?flag='. Signature verification, exact-byte cache keys (CDN cache policies), and legacy semicolon-separated parsers receive different input than the caller sent, even though the URL was already valid.
findings.summary: Running every query through URLSearchParams parse/re-serialize rewrites the raw query bytes of already-valid URLs, which is not semantics-preserving for servers that consume the query without form-decoding.

findings.failure_scenario: Running 'yarn test:snips' (apps/api/package.json) does not execute special-characters.test.ts because the glob's '*' does not cross directory separators; the suite that exists specifically to run these snippet tests reports green without exercising the new URL-validation regression tests (they only run under the default jest testMatch).
findings.summary: The new test is placed in a nested subdirectory that the dedicated 'test:snips' script glob (src/__tests__/snips/*.test.ts) does not match, so the snips suite silently skips this regression coverage.
